deviation_mechanism: High-reflectance broadband stacks rely on quarter-wave (QW) optical thickness staggering to accumulate a net π-phase shift per period. For SiO2/TiO2, the physical thickness ratio must satisfy t_low/t_high ≈ n_low/n_high ≈ 1.46/2.30 ≈ 0.63. Analyzing the executed candidate pool reveals systematic violations of this rule: candidate_thicknesses_nm[1] layers 0-1 yield 36.0/102.0 = 0.35; candidate_thicknesses_nm[3] layers 0-1 yield 41.0559269905957/89.23336917223283 = 0.46. These compressed low-index layers short-circuit the optical path difference, collapsing constructive interference outside the central wavelength and narrowing the stopband. The optimizer's continuous relaxation allowed adjacent layers to drift into non-resonant configurations, accumulating phase errors that cap the reflectance integral at ~0.80.
